title: Historical Aerial Photos of Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Where to see old aerial photos of your Berlin street, and how to read them.

items.q: Where can I see historical aerial photos of Berlin for free?
items.a: On **Geoportal Berlin**, the city's official map, and in the quicker **luftbilder.berlin.codefor.de** viewer that runs on the same open data. Both let you search for an address and switch between years.

items.q: Which year should I open for my street?
items.a: **1928** shows Berlin before the war, sharp enough to count courtyard wings. **1953** shows what the war left: cleared plots and outlines of blocks. Compare both with the **newest colour photo** of today.

items.q: Why does my street look blurry in 1953?
items.a: The 1953 flight was photographed at **1:22,000**, much smaller than the 1928 flight at 1:4,000. Zoom out a little and look at whole blocks rather than single houses.

items.q: Why is my street white in some years?
items.a: Each flight covered a different area. **1928 is nearly complete**, but the flight around **1938 covers only parts of the city**, and many flights between **1954 and 1989 cover only West Berlin**. Check the neighbouring years when one is blank.

items.q: Is there a straight line through my block in 1928?
items.a: The 1928 photos were taken as **separate sheets that do not overlap**. A sharp straight line where the grey tone jumps is usually a sheet edge, not a demolished row.

items.q: Can I use the photos, for example in a print or a school project?
items.a: Yes. Geoportal Berlin publishes the old flights under the **Datenlizenz Deutschland Zero**, which allows any use without asking and without naming the source, although naming it is good practice.

items.q: Can an aerial photo tell me who lived in my house?
items.a: No. It shows roofs, yards and streets. For residents, use the **Berlin address books**, which list every house and its tenants year by year until 1943.
